source_text: Ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς Ἐφέσιοι ἀπὸ Σμύρνης, ὅθεν καὶ γράφω ὑμῖν, παρόντες εἰς δόξαν θεοῦ, ὥσπερ καὶ ὑμεῖς οἲ κατὰ πάντα με ἀνέπαυσαν ἅμα Πολυκάρπῳ, ἐπισκόπῳ Σμυρναίων. καὶ αἱ λοιπαὶ δὲ ἐκκλησίαι ἐν τιμῇ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς. ἔρρωσθε ἐν ὁμονοίᾳ θεοῦ, κεκτημένοι ἀδιάκριτον πνεῦμα, ὅς ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός.
thought_title: Greetings from the Ephesians and other churches
orientation: Ignatius is closing his letter to the Magnesians, sending greetings from the Ephesians who are with him in Smyrna and from the other churches.
pass_a_gloss: The Ephesians from Smyrna greet you, from where also I write to you, being present for the glory of God, just as also you who in all things refreshed me together with Polycarp, bishop of the Smyrnaeans. And the remaining churches also in honor of Jesus Christ greet you. Farewell in the concord of God, possessing an undivided spirit, which is Jesus Christ.

choices.why: The adjective means not divided or not wavering; rendering it as 'undivided' keeps the sense of a spirit free from division, which fits Ignatius's emphasis on unity.
The glossary does not cover ὁμόνοια, but 'concord' preserves the sense of shared mind and unity that Ignatius urges, and 'of God' keeps the genitive as source or sphere.
The phrase indicates the manner or sphere in which the churches greet, and 'in honor of' keeps the dative sense of τιμή as the regard in which the greeting is made.
rejected: for the honor of Jesus Christ

choices.english: from where also I write to you
choices.why: The relative adverb indicates the place from which Ignatius writes, and 'also' preserves the καί, which links the Ephesians' presence to his writing.
rejected: whence I also write to you
from which place I write to you

pass_b_english: The Ephesians who are here in Smyrna, from where I am writing to you, greet you. They are present for the glory of God, and together with Polycarp, the bishop of the Smyrnaeans, they have refreshed me in every way, just as you have. The rest of the churches also greet you in the honor of Jesus Christ. Farewell in the harmony of God, possessing an undivided spirit, who is Jesus Christ.

problems.quote: and they have refreshed me in every way, together with Polycarp
problems.source_quote: ὥσπερ καὶ ὑμεῖς οἳ κατὰ πάντα με ἀνέπαυσαν ἅμα Πολυκάρπῳ
problems.why: English makes Ephesians refresh Ignatius; Greek says 'you' (addressees/Magnesians) did.
problems.fix: just as you are, you who refreshed me in every way together with Polycarp
problems.ruling: Greek ὑμεῖς ('you') is subject of ἀνέπαυσαν; English 'they' wrongly makes Ephesians the refreshers instead of addressees.

edits.old: They are present here for the glory of God, just as you also are, and they have refreshed me in every way, together with Polycarp, the bishop of the Smyrnaeans.
edits.new: They are present here for the glory of God, just as you also are, you who refreshed me in every way together with Polycarp, the bishop of the Smyrnaeans.

problems.why: Smyrna is called both 'Smyrna' and 'the Smyrnaeans'; readers may wonder if these differ.
problems.fix: Use 'Smyrna' consistently or explain that 'Smyrnaeans' means the church at Smyrna.

fixed: Changed 'the bishop of the Smyrnaeans' to 'the bishop of Smyrna' to avoid confusion between Smyrna and the Smyrnaeans, since the source refers to Polycarp as bishop of the Smyrnaeans, meaning the church at Smyrna.

last_rejected.quote: possessing an undivided spirit, which is Jesus Christ
last_rejected.source_quote: κεκτημένοι ἀδιάκριτον πνεῦμα, ὅς ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός
last_rejected.why: Relative pronoun ὅς is masculine, referring back to πνεῦμα (neuter) by attraction to predicate noun; 'which' should be 'who' since Jesus Christ is personal subject.
last_rejected.fix: possessing an undivided spirit, who is Jesus Christ
last_rejected.ruling: ὅς can be rendered 'which' referring to πνεῦμα; 'who' is preference, not a major error.

polish.changed: Clarified that the Ephesians are the ones who refreshed Ignatius, smoothed the sentence flow, and made the closing blessing read naturally.

notes.why: Smyrna is called both 'Smyrna' and 'the Smyrnaeans'; readers may wonder if these differ.
notes.fix: Use 'Smyrna' consistently or explain that 'Smyrnaeans' means the church at Smyrna.

polish.changed: Clarified that the Ephesians are in Smyrna with Ignatius, made the pronoun references explicit, and smoothed the sentence order for natural modern reading while preserving every claim and greeting.

notes.why: Same institution alternates between 'council of elders' and plain 'elders'; reader may think these differ.
notes.fix: Use consistent term or gloss as 'body of elders/presbyters'.

notes.quote: The Ephesians greet you from Smyrna
notes.why: City name appears before the letter to Smyrna is reached; reader may be confused.
notes.fix: No change needed; orientation covers Smyrna.
